questions.q: A sub-atomic particle of mass $10^{-30} \mathrm{~kg}$ is moving with a velocity $2.21 \times 10^6 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$. Under the matter wave consideration, the particle will behave closely like $\qquad  \left(\mathrm{h}=6.63 \times 10^{-34} \mathrm{~J} . \mathrm{s}\right)$
questions.subject: Physics

questions.q:
The stopping potential ${V}_{o}$ (in volt) as a function of frequency $( v )$ for a sodium emitter, is shown in the figure. The work function of sodium, form the data plotted in the figure, will be:
(Given: Planck’s constant \left(h\right) = 6.63 \times {10}^{- 34}Js$ , electron charge $( \text{e} )= 1.6 \times {10}^{- 19}C )$
$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$From Einstein's photoelectric equation, $hν = ϕ + e{V}_{0}$.

$⇒ {V}_{0} = \dfrac{hν}{e} - \dfrac{ϕ}{e} . . . . . . \left(1\right)$

At~$ν = 4 \times {10}^{14}Hz$,~${V}_{0} = 0$.

Putting the value in equation~ \left(1\right)$, we get

~$0 = $\dfrac{hv}{e} - \dfrac{ϕ}{e}

So,~Work function $( ϕ ) = $\dfrac{ \left(hν\right)}{e} \left(ineV\right)$
$= $\dfrac{6.63 \times {10}^{- 34} \times \left(4 \times {10}^{14}\right)}{1.6 \times {10}^{- 19}}
$= 1.66eV$

$

questions.q: The light of two different frequencies whose photons have energies $3 . 8eV$ and $1 . 4eV$ respectively, illuminate a metallic surface whose work function is $0 . 6eV$ successively. The ratio of maximum speeds of emitted electrons for the two frequencies respectively will be :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Expression for maximum kinetic energy can be written as,& \left(KE\right)max = E - ϕ$

\left(KE\right)max, 1 = {E}_{1} - ϕ = 3 . 8 - 0 . 6 = 3 . 2eV$,~\left(KE\right)max, 2 = {E}_{2} - ϕ = 1 . 4 - 0 . 6 = 0 . 8eV$

$\dfrac{\left(KE\right)max, 1}{\left(KE\right)max, 2} = \dfrac{3 . 2}{0 . 8} = 4 ⇒ 4 = \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{2}{mv}_{1}^{2}}{\dfrac{1}{2}m{v}_{2}^{2}}$~

$⇒ {v}_{1}^{2}{v}_{2}^{2} = 4$~$⇒ \dfrac{v1}{v2} = 2: 1$

$

questions.q: The work function of a substance is $3 . 0eV$. The longest wavelength of light that can cause the emission of photoelectrons from this substance is approximately:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For longest wavelength, the emitted electron will have nearly zero kinetic energy.

Therefore,

$\lambda = \dfrac{hc}{We}$

$⇒ \lambda = \dfrac{1240nm - eV}{3eV}$

$⇒ \lambda = 413 . 33nm$

$⇒ {λ}_\max \approx 414nm$

questions.q: Electron beam used in an electron microscope, when accelerated by a voltage of $20kV$~has a de-Broglie wavelength of~${λ}_{0}$. If the voltage is increased to $40kV$& then the de-Broglie wavelength associated with the electron beam would be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The de-Broglie wavelength of an electron accelerated through potential& $V$~is~

$\lambda = \dfrac{h}{mv} = \dfrac{h}{2m ( KE )} = \dfrac{h}{2meV}$

where,~$h$~is Planck's constant,~$e$~is charge of electron~and~$m$~is mass of electron.

From above relation,~$\lambda ∝ \dfrac{1}{V}$

$∴ \dfrac{λ}{\lambda0} = \sqrt{\dfrac{20}{40}}$

$⇒ \lambda = \dfrac{\lambda0}{2}$.

questions.q: In a photoelectric effect experiment, the graph of stopping potential $V$ versus reciprocal of wavelength obtained is shown in the figure. As the intensity of incident radiation is increased :&
options: Slope of the straight line get more steep
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Einstein's photoelectric equation is given by,

${eV}_{s} = hν - {W}_{o}$, where~${W}_{o}$~is the work function.

$⇒ {V}_{s} = \dfrac{hc}{eλ} - \dfrac{Wo}{e}$, where~$c = ν\lambda$.

Intensity does not affect the frequency and work function of a material. Therefore,& the graph does not change with increasing intensity.

questions.q: Consider an electron in a hydrogen atom, revolving in its second excited state (having radius $4.65\text{Å}$ ). The de-Broglie wavelength of this electron is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
According to Bohr’s atomic model
$mvr = \dfrac{nh}{2\pi}$
And the de-Broglie wavelength
$\lambda = \dfrac{h}{mv}$
From the above two equations we can write, $\lambda = \dfrac{2\pir}{n}$
In the 2nd excited state
$\lambda = \dfrac{2\pir}{3}$
$∴ \lambda = \dfrac{2}{3}\pi \times 4.65Å = 9.7Å$

questions.q: Two sources of light emit with a power of $200W$. The ratio of number of photons of visible light emitted by each source having wavelengths $300$ nm and $500$ nm respectively, will be :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let ${n}_{1}$ and ${n}_{2}$ be the number of photons coming out from the first and the second source of light respectively per second.

So, for the first source,

${n}_{1} \times \dfrac{hc}{\lambda1} = 200 . . . \left(1\right)$

And, for the second source,

${n}_{2} \times $\dfrac{hc}{\lambda2} =$200 . . . \left(2\right)$

From equations (1) and (2), it implies that

$\dfrac{n1}{n2} = \dfrac{\lambda1}{\lambda2} = \dfrac{300}{500}⇒ \dfrac{n1}{n2} = \dfrac{3}{5}$

questions.q: A proton, a neutron, an electron and an $\alpha$-particle have same energy. If ${λ}_{p}, {λ}_{n}, {λ}_{e}$ and ${λ}_{α}$ are the de Broglie's wavelengths of proton, neutron, electron and $\alpha$& particle respectively, then choose the correct relation from the following&
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The de-Broglie wavelength $\lambda = \dfrac{h}{2m ( K . E . )}$

where,~$h$ and $K . E .$~are~constant

$\lambda ∝ \dfrac{1}{m}$

$m =$~Mass of the particle

Thus, with increasing mass of particle de-Broglie wavelength decreases.

Order of mass~${m}_{e} < {m}_{p} < {m}_{n} < {m}_{α}$

Order of de-Broglie wavelength is~${λ}_{a} < {λ}_{n} < {λ}_{p} < {λ}_{e}$

questions.q:
If a source of electromagnetic radiation having power $15kW$ produces ${10}^{16}$ photons per second, the radiation belongs to a part of spectrum is :

(Take Planck constant $h = 6 \times {10}^{- 34}Js )$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As energy of one photon is given by& $E = \dfrac{Power}{Photonfrequency}$

Or,~$E = hν = \dfrac{15 \times {10}^{3}}{1016}$

So, frequency of ray is~$ν = \dfrac{15 \times {10}^{- 13}}{6 \times {10}^{- 34}} = 2 . 5 \times {10}^{21}Hz$.

Thus, the radiation belongs to gamma rays.

.

questions.q: A particle moving with kinetic energy $E$ has de Broglie wavelength $\lambda$ . If energy $\Delta E$ is added to its energy, the wavelength become $\dfrac{\lambda}{2}$ . Value of $\Delta E,$ is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\lambda = \dfrac{h}{2\left(KE\right)m} ⇒ \lambda ∝ \dfrac{1}{KE}$
$\dfrac{\lambda}{\dfrac{\lambda}{2}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{KE{}_{f}}{K{E}_{i}}}$
$4K{E}_{i} = K{E}_{f}$
$⇒ \Delta E = 4K{E}_{i} - K{E}_{i} = 3KE = 3E$

questions.q: A small mirror of mass $m$ is suspended by a massless thread of length $l$. Then the small angle through which the thread will be deflected when a short pulse of laser of energy $E$ falls normal on the mirror ( $\mathrm{c}=$ speed of light in vacuum and $\mathrm{g}=$ acceleration due to gravity)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Force due to beam assuming complete reflection $\mathrm{F}=\frac{2 \mathrm{P}}{\mathrm{C}}=\frac{2}{\mathrm{C}} \frac{\mathrm{dE}}{\mathrm{dt}} ; \mathrm{P}$ is power
So change in momentum of mirror.
$\mathrm{m}(\mathrm{~V}-0)=\int \mathrm{Fdt}=\frac{2}{\mathrm{C}} \int \mathrm{dE}=\frac{2 \mathrm{E}}{\mathrm{C}}$
Now using work energy theorem ...(1)
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{W}_{\mathrm{g}}=\Delta \mathrm{k} \\ & -\mathrm{mg} \ell(1-\cos \theta)=0-\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{mv}^2 \\ & \mathrm{~g} \ell\left(2 \sin ^2 \frac{\theta}{2}\right)=\frac{\mathrm{v}^2}{2}
\end{aligned}$
as $\theta$ is small
$\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{g} \ell 2\left(\frac{\theta}{2}\right)^2=\frac{1}{2} \frac{4 \mathrm{E}^2}{\mathrm{~m}^2 \mathrm{c}^2} \\ & \mathrm{~g} \ell \theta^2=\frac{4 \mathrm{E}^2}{\mathrm{~m}^2 \mathrm{c}^2} \\ & \theta=\frac{2 \mathrm{E}}{\mathrm{mc} \sqrt{\mathrm{g} \ell}}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: If the total energy transferred to a surface in time $t$ is $6 . 48 \times {10}^{5}J$, then the magnitude of the total momentum delivered to this surface for complete absorption will be :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As we know,

$p = \dfrac{E}{c},$ where $c$ is velocity of light.

Therefore, $p = \dfrac{6 . 48 \times {10}^{5}}{3 \times {10}^{8}} = 2 . 16 \times {10}^{- 3}kgms^{- 1}$

questions.q: A particle $'P'$ is formed due to a completely inelastic collision of particles $'x'$ and $'y'$ having de-Broglie wavelengths $'{\lambda}_{x}'$ and $'{\lambda}_{y}'$ respectively. If $x$ and $y$ were moving in opposite directions, then the de-Broglie wavelength of $'P'$ is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\dfrac{h}{\lambda} = \left|\dfrac{h}{{\lambda}_{x}} - \dfrac{h}{{\lambda}_{y}}\right|$
$\dfrac{1}{\lambda} = \left|\dfrac{1}{{\lambda}_{x}} - \dfrac{1}{{\lambda}_{y}}\right|$
$\lambda = \dfrac{{\lambda}_{x}{\lambda}_{y}}{\left|{\lambda}_{x} - {\lambda}_{y}\right|}$

questions.q: An electron with speed $v$ and a photon with speed~$c$ have the same de-Broglie wavelength. If the kinetic energy and momentum of electron are ${E}_{e}$ and ${P}_{e}$ and that of photon are ${E}_{ph}$ and ${P}_{ph}$& respectively. Which of the following is correct?
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
We have,& ${λ}_{p} = \dfrac{h}{pp}$~and~${λ}_{e} = \dfrac{h}{pe}$

Given here,~${λ}_{e} = {λ}_{p}$, then~${p}_{p} = {p}_{e}$

Ratio of their energy is~$\dfrac{Eph}{Ee} = \dfrac{\dfrac{hc}{\lambdaP}}{{p}_e^{2}2m} = \dfrac{2mc}{pe} = \dfrac{2mc}{mv} = \dfrac{2c}{v}$

questions.q: A light source of wavelength $\lambda$ illuminates a metal surface and electrons are ejected with maximum kinetic energy of 2 eV . If the same surface is illuminated by a light source of wavelength $\frac{\lambda}{2}$, then the maximum kinetic energy of ejected electrons will be (The work function of metal is 1 eV )
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Einstein's photoelectric equation
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{KE}=\frac{h c}{\lambda}=\phi_0 \\
& 2 \mathrm{eV}=\frac{h c}{\lambda}-1 \mathrm{eV} \\
& \frac{h c}{\lambda}=3 \mathrm{eV} \\
& \mathrm{KE}^{\prime}=\frac{h c}{(\lambda / 2)}-\phi_0=6 \mathrm{eV}-1 \mathrm{eV}
\end{aligned}=5 \mathrm{eV}$

questions.q: An electron of mass $m$ and magnitude of charge $e$~at rest, gets accelerated by a constant electric field $E$.~The rate of change of de-Broglie wavelength of this electron at a time $t$& is (ignore relativistic effects)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The acceleration of the electron is

$a = \dfrac{eE}{m}$

The velocity of the electron as a function of time is

$v = at = \dfrac{eE}{m}t$

The de-Broglie wavelength is

$\lambda = \dfrac{h}{mv}$

$\lambda = \dfrac{h}{m\left(\dfrac{eE}{m}\right)t}$

$\lambda = \dfrac{h}{eEt}$
$\dfrac{d\lambda}{dt} = - \dfrac{h}{eEt^{2}}$

questions.q: A beam of electromagnetic radiation of intensity $6.4 \times {10}^{- 5} \text{W} / {\text{cm}}^{2}$ is comprised of wavelength, $\lambda = 310nm$ . It falls normally on a metal (work function $\phi = 2eV$ ) of surface area of $1{cm}^{2}$ . If one in ${10}^{3}$ photons ejects an election, total number of electrons ejected in $1s$ is ${10}^{x}$ . \left(hc = 1240eVnm, 1eV = 1.6 \times {10}^{- 19}J\right),$ then $x is ___________
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Energy of photon. $E = \dfrac{1240}{310\left(\text{nm}\right)} = 4eV > 2eV$ (So photoelectric effect will take place)
$= 4 \times 1.6 \times {10}^{- 19} = 6.4 \times {10}^{- 19}joule$
Number of photons falling per second
$= \dfrac{6.4 \times {10}^{- 5} \times 1}{6.4 \times {10}^{- 19}} = {10}^{14}$
Number of photoelectron emitted per second
$= \dfrac{{10}^{14}}{{10}^{3}} = {10}^{11}$

questions.q:
A light beam of wavelength $500$ nm is incident on a metal having work function of $1 . 25eV$, placed in a magnetic field of intensity $B$. The electrons emitted perpendicular to the magnetic field $B$, with maximum kinetic energy are bent into a circular arc of radius $30$ cm. The value of $B$ is ________\times {10}^{- 7}T$.
Given $hc = 20 \times {10}^{- 26}Jm$, the mass of the electron$= 9 \times {10}^{- 31}kg.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
By photoelectric equation

$\dfrac{hc}{λ} - ϕ = {k}_\max$

${k}_\max = \dfrac{1240}{500} - 1 . 25 \approx 1 . 25$

$r = \dfrac{2mk}{eB}$

$B = \dfrac{2mk}{er}$

$= 125 \times {10}^{- 7}T$
